bib.title: LLMs Can Plan Only If We Tell Them

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LLMs Can Plan Only If We Tell Them" (AoT+), Bilgehan Sel, Ruoxi Jia, Ming Jin (Virginia Tech). ICLR 2025 (arXiv 2501.13545v1, 23 Jan 2025).

COVERAGE: 109,754 chars extracted. I read about 0-84,000 in full (body, references skimmed, Appendix A, prompts B.1-B.4) and the last ~1,500 chars. I did NOT read about 84,000-108,000 (ACRE and List Functions prompt text, B.5-B.6), which is prompt text only. I checked it for limitations, instance counts and temperature, and found none. Partial read of prompt appendices only; all results tables and the text are covered. Extraction is clean.

FIT WARNING: Moderate. The paper is about prompting for planning (search traces plus state restatement), not tool use or ReAct. It has no tool-calling agent loop and no plan-and-execute. It does give numbers against ToT (Game of 24, crosswords, creative writing only), CoT, Self-Refine, Tree-Planner and LLM-Modulo (the external-verifier baseline). It fits the planning-strategies section (ToT, plan-and-execute contrast) better than notes/02-tool-use-and-react.md. The paper has no Limitations section.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. AoT+ beats LLM-Modulo (external verifier loop) on Blocksworld with most models, in a single prompt.
 number: GPT-4 82 vs 82; GPT-4o 73 vs 48; Claude 82 vs 19 (Blocksworld). Logistics GPT-4 80 vs 70.
 setup: Blocksworld/Logistics via PDDL validity (Valmeekam et al. 2023 setup); LLM-Modulo run with its own code base. Appendix A.5 says LLM-Modulo is partly "optimization for GPT-4, their primary LLM". Instance counts and the number of runs are not stated in the text I read.
 quote: "Blocksworld CoT 35 34 43 8 -16-4 4 -6-25 / LLM-Modulo 82 48 19 3-4-0 0-13-34 / AoT 45 43 66 8-23-25 3-17 -35 / AoT+ 82 73 82 27 -39-46 5 -52-77" (column order GPT-4, GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini 1.5 8B/Flash/Pro, LLaMA 3.1 8B/70B/405B)
 where: Table 3, p9. Same numbers in Table 5, p17.
2. AoT+ cuts CoT's weakness: Blocksworld CoT 35 (GPT-4) goes to 82. The paper says CoT gives "little to no improvement" on Blocksworld, and GPT-4 gets about 30%. Human baseline is 78%.
 number: 35 -> 82 (GPT-4); Logistics CoT 14 -> AoT+ 80 (GPT-4).
 setup: as above.
 quote: "in benchmarks like Blocksworld, where human performance reaches approximately 78% accuracy, even state-of-the-art models like GPT-4 achieve only around 30% accuracy, with CoT prompting offering little to no improvement." Also "It also surpasses human performance of 78% (Valmeekam et al., 2023) in the Blocksworld domain when GPT-4 or Claude is used."
 where: p2 and p10.
3. The gain comes from state memoization, not from human-written heuristics. Ablation, GPT-4 Blocksworld: AoT 45, AoT+R (random traces only) 44, AoT+M (memoization only) 84, AoT+ (both) 82. Logistics: AoT 24, AoT+R 24, AoT+M 80, AoT+ 80.
 setup: Table 5, ablation of the two changes. Memoization means periodically restating and caching the current state with identifiers x.y.z after each step.
 quote: "AoT+R do have very close performance to AoT, whereas AoT+M, or we can think of it AoT+ with human intuitions, getting similar performance to AoT+."
 where: Table 5, p17.
4. Token cost: AoT+ uses roughly 3x fewer total tokens than LLM-Modulo on Blocksworld and about 4x fewer on Logistics. It uses more than CoT (about 3x on Blocksworld, 4.7x on Logistics).
 number: GPT-4 mean tokens per problem. Blocksworld total: CoT 650.7, AoT 1929.5, LLM-Modulo 6452.9, AoT+ 2067.8. Logistics total: CoT 1205.1, AoT 4472.6, LLM-Modulo 23015.3, AoT+ 5606.1.
 quote: "AoT+ demonstrates significantly lower token usage, with alternative methods requiring more than 3 times the total tokens." Also "LLM-Modulo methods taking on average more than 6 times longer to complete the benchmarks."
 where: Table 4 p10; Table 6 (with std) p17. The wall-clock claim is hedged by the authors for internet latency. No call counts are given. The paper does not report the number of LLM-Modulo iterations.
5. State hallucination grows with solution depth under plain AoT and is much lower under AoT+.
 number: Fig 4 curve only (error rate 0 to 1 over depth 1-20). I have no point values.
 setup: Logistics, LLaMA 3.1 70B, 200 games, 20 sampled states per depth, an error being a stated state that differs from replaying the proposed actions.
 quote: "we conducted an experiment to analyze the error rates for states for AoT and AoT+ in the Logistics benchmark using LLaMA 3.1 70B model."
 where: App A.1, p16.
6. Versus ToT (Game of 24, crosswords, creative writing): AoT matches or beats ToT with one query, and the random-trace version loses little.
 number: Game of 24: CoT-SC 9.0, ToT 69.0, AoT 71.0, AoT+R 70.0. Crosswords: 15.6, 46.5, 52.0, 54.0. Creative writing score: 6.93, 7.56, 7.58, 7.59.
 setup: CoT-SC with 10 samples. Model not stated in the text I read.
 quote: "Method Game of 24 Crossword Puzzle Creative Writing / CoT-SC 9.0% 15.6% 6.93 / ToT 69.0% 46.5% 7.56 / AoT 71.0% 52.0% 7.58 / AoT+R 70.0% 54.0% 7.59"
 where: Table 1, p7. These are the ToT numbers. They are not Blocksworld numbers, so the ToT baseline is the original paper's setup.
7. Self-Refine and Tree-Planner are weak baselines (Blocksworld GPT-4): Self-Refine (10 iterations, with external-validator feedback) 39 vs CoT 35. Tree-Planner (N=25, up to 10 corrections) 44.
 quote: "Self-Refine demonstrates only marginal improvements over the CoT baseline".
 where: App A.4-A.5, p17-18, Table 5. Tree-Planner needs action reversibility; the authors note this may be infeasible in non-ergodic settings.
8. Scale effect: gains are larger for bigger models; small models gain little. Examples are Blocksworld AoT+ Gemini 1.5 8B 27 and LLaMA 3.1 8B 5, vs LLaMA 405B 77. Open-weight 405B is near GPT-4 under AoT+ (77 vs 82) but not under LLM-Modulo (34).
 quote: "The gains of AoT+ are more substantial with larger models, revealing an emergent ability for planning as the scale of the models increases."
 where: p10.
9. Inductive tasks also improve (GPT-4): List Functions CoT 38, LLM-Modulo 70, AoT 58, AoT+ 84. ACRE CoT 28, LLM-Modulo 52, AoT 46, AoT+ 72. Table 3, p9.
10. Mechanism evidence (weak): on LLaMA-2-13B-chat, the share of attention on solution steps drops from 86.3% (AoT) to 27.0% (AoT+) on Blocksworld, and from 78.5% to 26.3% on List Functions.
 quote: "Method Blocksworld List Functions / AoT 86.3% 78.5% / AoT+ 27.0% 26.3%"
 where: Table 2, p7. The caption says the share is "over the solution steps (in opposed to the problem definition and/or initial and goal state definitions)". The authors read this as more access to relevant state.

BASELINES (compute matched?): Not matched. LLM-Modulo and Tree-Planner are multi-call; AoT+ is a single query. Token counts are given only for GPT-4 on Blocksworld/Logistics, and only against CoT, AoT and LLM-Modulo. CoT is run with 5-shot prompts; the Game of 24 CoT-SC uses 10 samples. No equal-token CoT-SC comparison on planning. No LLM-Modulo iteration cap or success-vs-iterations curve is reported in the text I read. Self-Refine used temperature 0.7 and a 5-shot setting. Statistical significance, seeds and instance counts are not reported (stds only for tokens). LLM-Modulo may be tuned for GPT-4, which makes the non-GPT-4 gaps (Claude 19 vs 82) suspect as a baseline-setup effect.

LIMITS: The paper has no limitations section. Authors concede the following:
- Original AoT prompts are hard to craft.
- Hand-written heuristics can bias search.
- State hallucination persists in plain AoT.
- Tree-Planner needs reversible actions.
- LLM-Modulo is tuned for GPT-4.
Not shown:
- Real tool use or ReAct-style environments.
- Planning with unknown or dynamic state (the state is restated by the model itself, so errors can compound).
- Larger Blocksworld depths.
- Sound verification: AoT+ gives no guarantee, whereas LLM-Modulo has a verifier.
- Reasoning-trained models (o1-style); dated by 2026 since the models are GPT-4, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5-era, Gemini 1.5 and LLaMA 3.1.
- Whether the 82% "beats human" holds up: the human number comes from Valmeekam 2023.
The attention analysis uses a different model (LLaMA-2-13B) from the main results. The AoT+ prompts are hand-built per domain with 4-5 examples.

BUILDS ON: Algorithm of Thoughts (Sel et al., 2024b); Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al., 2024); CoT (Wei et al., 2022; Kojima et al., 2022); Self-Consistency (Wang et al., 2022); LLM-Modulo (Kambhampati et al., 2024); Valmeekam et al. (2023) for Blocksworld/Logistics setup; Stechly et al. (2023, 2024) on self-verification; Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2024); Tree-Planner (Hu et al., 2023); ReAct (Yao et al., 2022, cited only in the introduction); Lost in the Middle (Liu et al., 2024a) as the motivation for restating state; Qiu et al. (2023) for ACRE/List Functions.

CODE (prompt templates worth keeping; B.3 AoT+ Blocksworld, p23-27):
- System prompt lists the actions and preconditions, then ends: "Also, in the last part, do not use a numbered list or something to return the actions, just return them like in the examples. Use 'The PDDL version: bla bla' to return the PDDL code, and do not add anything after the actions."
- Few-shot answer format with state after each step and backtracking:
 "1. Pick-up D / 2. Stack D on C. C is not clear. Backtracking... / 1. Unstack B from C / 2. Put-down B / - A on table, B on table, C on table, D on table. / Now that all blocks are on the table, we just have to follow the initial plan of ours."
- Memoization format (Fig 3): "1. Unstack A from B and Stack A on D: B on C on T, A on D on E on T." then "1.1. Unstack B from C and Put-down B: ..." then "Backtracking to 1.:" then "1.2 ...". Each action line is followed by the full restated state, and node ids (x.y.z) let the model jump back to a visited node.
- Self-Refine validator prompt (B.2): "[CHECK] The above plan is invalid. The following action at step 1 has an unmet precondition: ... The unmet precondition is: ..."

FIGURE candidate: Figure 3, p8. AoT vs AoT+ on one Blocksworld problem side by side: the AoT trace marks a "STATE ERROR", while the AoT+ trace restates the state after every action with node ids (1, 1.1, 1.1.1, "Backtracking to 1."). It shows the whole mechanism faster than prose. Alternates: Fig 1 (p2, AoT+ vs LLM-Modulo diagram, text-only extraction), Fig 4 (p16, state error vs depth).

PROBLEMS: Figure text in the extraction is scattered (Fig 1 labels, Fig 3 words one per line). Table 3 column headers are garbled ("Gemini 1.58B-Flash-Pro" means 1.5 8B/Flash/Pro; "LLaMA 3.18B-70B-405B" means 3.1 8B/70B/405B). The Gemini and LLaMA triples are read as sizes in that order. Pages 41+ of the PDF contain prompts only and were not read in full (the ACRE/List Functions prompt block, about 84k-108k chars). No embedded instructions found in the text. The Logistics total for AoT+ (5606.1) is not the sum of the printed Input and Output (2879.4+1726.7=4606.1), so one of the three printed numbers is wrong (Tables 4 and 6 agree with each other); use with care.
